value: A Haiku builder would ask: (1) Where? cairn/devices/tester/hollow.py: a new `_first_build_commit(tid, files, since_at, repo_root)` runs `git log --reverse --format=%H --grep=<tid> --since=<the bounding back-edge at, or none> -- <files>` and returns the first hash or None; measure() takes `commit = prebuild_commit(at)`, and if the first build commit exists and is an ancestor of that commit (`git merge-base --is-ancestor`), it uses `<first>^` instead and sets anchor_rule='first-build-commit'. Otherwise anchor_rule='journal'. (2) Which back-edge bounds? `cairn.tools.base.crossings.crossings_for(tid, roots)` lists every crossing with `direction`; take the back-edges (direction 'back', from BUILDME or PROVEME) and choose the LATEST one after which at least one build commit exists; a back-edge with no build commit after it is a retreat-and-recross and is skipped; none qualifying means no bound. List the build commits once (`git log --reverse --format=%H%x20%cI --grep=<tid> -- <files>`) and choose in Python. (3) What does the reading gain? `anchor: {rule, commit, journal_commit, first_build_commit}`, sealed with the rest through record_hollow. (4) The unmeasurable case? After the per-file loop, if measured is empty and every non-skipped file was UNWRIT, raise HollowUnmeasurable('hollow: every eligible file is identical at <commit> — the anchor postdates the build, not the chart'); the cli already prints HollowUnmeasurable and exits nonzero. (5) Proof? cairn/devices/tester/proofs/test_hollow_anchor.py, four teeth over scratch git repos built in tmp dirs with a scratch journal: build-before-crossing anchors at the build's parent; kickback-and-rebuild anchors at the rebuild's parent; build-then-retreat-and-recross (no rebuild) anchors at the original build's parent; all-identical raises. Sealed by the tester. (6) Then run `cairn test --hollow 68f563403c8f --seal` and `cairn test --hollow c691e19d5464 --seal` live and recompute the clearance lacks.
